source_snapshot.procedure: Run `ipmitool chassis power off`; after the system is off use `ipmitool chassis power status` and require off; then run `ipmitool chassis power on`; after the system is on use `ipmitool chassis power status` and require on.
source_snapshot.criteria: All step responses are correct and the system powers on/off normally.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL proposes only `chassis power on` followed by the broader `chassis status`, with cipher 17 and password arguments; it omits the source off transition and off-state proof.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly requires a CRITICAL, explicitly authorized off/status/on/status sequence with workload protection, bounded polling, boot health, evidence and recovery.

old_problem: The prior record kept Pending for target, outage, hard-versus-graceful off choice, timings and recovery. The source itself resolves the command semantic: this case specifically covers standard IPMI Chassis Control Power Down followed by Power Up, while the adjacent Power Soft variant separately covers graceful shutdown. Remaining target, maintenance and recovery values are bounded execution parameters.
disposition_reason: Preserve the exact source sequence and do not replace its hard `power off` with graceful/soft shutdown. In an isolated, recoverable SUT with no active workload or writes, separately authorize one standard Power Down, prove stable Off, then separately authorize one Power Up and prove On through POST and OS Ready/service health. The DeepSeek power-on-only sequence is incomplete. Every failure stops without retry and retains logs.
decision_basis: XLSX row 983, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 984 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 984 / variant b68f0e7394ae9672.

IPMI v2.0 defines Chassis Control command 0x02 with control values Power Down and Power Up, and separately defines Get Chassis Status Current Power State. These standard semantics are sufficient to write the review-layer command/state checks without inventing OEM behavior.

Pinned ipmitool maps the source `off`/`on` subcommands to standard Down/Off and Up/On control values; command completion is only acknowledgement and must be followed by the canonical power-state observation.

The next source row is explicitly `Power Soft`; therefore substituting a graceful action here would erase the distinct hard-off coverage. Data-integrity risk is controlled through a dedicated nonproduction/recoverable image, workload and I/O quiescence, explicit hard-off authorization and an incident recovery path.

ED-06, ED-15, ED-17, ED-18, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 preserve transition identity, objective acceptance, evidence, full Off→On→OS Ready recovery and per-case analysis; ED-33 through ED-38 allow parameterized execution only with staged confirmation, protected tools and no retry.

test_case.test_name: Verify one authorized IPMI hard power-down and power-up through OS Ready
test_case.purpose: Verify the bound SUT accepts the standard IPMI chassis Power Down and later Power Up controls, reaches a stable Off state, and then completes the full recovery path to On, POST and OS Ready/service health, without conflating this hard-off case with Power Soft, reset, DC cycle or AC cycle.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/console identity and approved protected IPMI path with pinned ipmitool, parser and reviewed Script revision
Dedicated nonproduction or explicitly outage-approved SUT, drained workloads, quiesced application/storage writes, verified backup/recovery and owner acceptance of abrupt Power Down risk
Captured baseline power, BMC, console, storage, filesystem, service and alarm health; original/final required state
Approved Off stabilization, On transition, POST, OS Ready and service-health timeouts with exact state parser and expected event allowlist
Secret-safe credential provider, maintenance window, two staged approvals, OOB console access and named recovery/operator ownership
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED HYBRID PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Verify exact SUT/BMC/console identity, preserve logs, capture healthy On baseline, drain workloads and quiesce writes while keeping the SUT in the source-required On pre-state. After explicit hard-off approval, use the approved secret-safe IPMI path to issue exactly one `chassis power off`. Record acknowledgement but judge transition only by bounded canonical `chassis power status` polling plus console/loss-of-host evidence until stable Off; stop if Off is not proven. After a new explicit power-on approval, issue exactly one `chassis power on`, poll canonical status to On, then observe console POST and wait through the approved OS Ready/service/storage/health gates. Preserve all expected and unexpected logs without clearing. Verify the owner-approved final state. Never substitute `soft`, reset, cycle or AC removal, and never automatically repeat either power command.
test_case.expected_result: From a verified safe On baseline, the one authorized Power Down is acknowledged and the same SUT reaches stable Off within timeout. The separately authorized Power Up is acknowledged, the same SUT reaches On, completes POST and reaches the approved OS Ready/service/storage/health state within timeout. Expected power events are present, no unexplained faults or data-integrity issues occur, and the final state is approved.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires both source transitions in order: On→stable Off after exactly one hard-off control, then Off→On→POST→OS Ready/service health after exactly one power-up control, with exact target, staged approvals, canonical state evidence, retained logs and approved final state. Power-on-only evidence, command acknowledgement alone, `chassis status` substitution, graceful soft-off, reset, cycle, AC interruption, or recovery evidence from another variant cannot pass. Wrong target, active workload/write risk, timeout, ambiguous state, failed boot/health/storage, unexpected logs or inability to reach the final state is FAIL; missing approved runtime inputs is NOT READY rather than Engineering Decision Pending.
safety_gate: Require explicit approval immediately before the hard Power Down and again before Power Up; reverify exact SUT/BMC identity and current state at both gates.
Run only on a dedicated/recoverable system or under an approved outage after workload drain and I/O quiescence; do not claim that hard off is graceful or data-safe by default.
Preserve SEL, console, OS and service evidence before action and throughout recovery; do not clear logs.
Use secret-safe credentials, bounded state polling and an allowlisted fixed sequence; deny arbitrary commands, reset, cycle, soft-off and policy changes.
Stop on first target, transition, console, storage, filesystem, service, thermal or alarm anomaly. Do not automatically retry or proceed from unproven Off to Power Up.
Keep OOB recovery and a named human operator available; any extraordinary recovery power action requires a new incident authorization outside this test.
expected_evidence: Two staged approvals, immutable SUT/BMC/console identity, maintenance window, hard-off risk acceptance and final-state requirement
On baseline, workload-drain/I/O-quiescence and backup/recovery readiness evidence
Redacted one-time Power Down acknowledgement plus timestamped canonical transition to stable Off
Redacted one-time Power Up acknowledgement plus power On, console POST, OS Ready and service/storage/health timeline
Preserved SEL/OS/console alarms and expected-event comparison, no-retry audit, final state and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On any anomaly, stop without repeating power controls and preserve all evidence. If the SUT is verified Off, keep it in the owner-defined safe state until the named recovery operator authorizes one incident-recovery start; if it is On but boot or storage health fails, use OOB console and the Project boot/storage recovery runbook without another cycle. Validate filesystems/storage/services and restore the approved final state before closing; escalate unresolved data-integrity or availability failures.

source_conflict.reason: The Master clearly requires off/status/on/status. DeepSeek's power-on-only implementation is rejected as incomplete guidance, not treated as an authoritative conflict.

blocked.reason: Standard IPMI defines Power Down, Power Up and Current Power State. Target, outage, quiescence, timeouts, boot criteria and recovery ownership are finite Project prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Exact SUT/BMC/console map; protected IPMI access; dedicated/outage context; workload/I/O quiescence and backup; Off/On/POST/OS/service timers; event allowlist; final state and incident recovery runbook.

project_authority: The Project owner supplies the exact target and access path, authorizes the abrupt outage on a recoverable SUT, defines quiescence, timeouts, boot/service health and final state, and owns incident recovery.
